<h1 id="2/d/solution">Solution</h1>

↑ **Parent:** [D](../d.md)

**No. Strict room values do not remove the [allocation externalities](../../../../../allocation-externality.md) generated by friends.** Consider the following new instance, with the same friendship pairs $\{S_1,S_4\}$ and $\{S_2,S_3\}$ and friendship bonus $0.4$ for each student:

$$
\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
 &r_1&r_2&r_3&r_4\\ \hline
S_1&0.50&0.30&0.02&0.01\\
S_2&0.01&0.50&0.30&0.02\\
S_3&0.01&0.70&0.02&0.50\\
S_4&0.01&0.50&0.02&0.03
\end{array}
$$

Each row is strictly ranked and every room value is positive. In picking order $S_1,S_2,S_3,S_4$, [backward induction](../../../../../backward-induction.md) gives the following continuations. Room numbers in a tuple are listed in student order.

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
S_1\text{ choice}&\text{resulting assignment}&U_1\\ \hline
r_1&(r_1,r_3,r_2,r_4)&0.50\\
r_2&(r_2,r_3,r_4,r_1)&0.70\\
r_3&(r_3,r_2,r_4,r_1)&0.02\\
r_4&(r_4,r_2,r_3,r_1)&0.01
\end{array}
$$

To check $S_2$'s incentives behind these continuations, the resulting [utilities](../../../../../utility.md) for their available choices, in ascending room order, are respectively $(0.50,0.70,0.02)$, $(0.01,0.70,0.42)$, $(0.41,0.50,0.02)$ and $(0.41,0.90,0.70)$. Student $S_3$'s own [best responses](../../../../../best-response.md) determine those figures, and $S_4$ again takes the remaining room. All comparisons selecting these continuations are strict.

Hence $S_1$ chooses $r_2$ and the [subgame perfect equilibrium](../../../../../subgame-perfect-equilibrium.md) outcome is

$$
a=(r_2,r_3,r_4,r_1),\qquad U(a)=(0.70,0.70,0.90,0.41).
$$

But the feasible assignment

$$
a'=(r_1,r_3,r_4,r_2),\qquad U(a')=(0.90,0.70,0.90,0.90)
$$

strictly improves $S_1$ and $S_4$ and leaves $S_2,S_3$ unchanged. Thus $a$ is not [Pareto optimal](../../../../../pareto-efficiency.md). This is compatible with equilibrium: a [Pareto improvement](../../../../../pareto-improvement.md) can require several players' actions to change. If $S_1$ alone takes $r_1$, the later [best responses](../../../../../best-response.md) lead to $(r_1,r_3,r_2,r_4)$, not to $a'$; anticipating that reaction gives $S_1$ only $0.50$.
